title: Third-language beginner module start (≥ 5 lessons + exercises; language partner-driven)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The third language demonstrates that the language-agnostic model scales beyond two languages. The choice of language is partner-driven (SQL for data beginners, a typed teaching language, or C basics are candidates). The in-browser runner viability for the third language must be confirmed by a spike before committing to the module.
objective: Author at least 5 lessons in a third programming language (chosen with partner input), each with at least one graded exercise, using the existing schema and runner contract without changes — demonstrating the language-agnostic model at scale.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 5 lessons are delivered in a third programming language (language chosen in consultation with the partner; document the rationale).
In-browser runner viability for the third language is confirmed by a spike before lesson authoring commits.
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with solutionVerified:true and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
No schema changes are required to accommodate the third language; only a new runner adapter is added.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson.
Technical + pedagogy review by non-authors for all lessons.
output: At least 5 merged lesson documents (with exercise files) for the third-language beginner module, each schema-valid, correctness-verified, and reviewed.
